environmentNote: This automated tab persistently reports document.hidden === true / visibilityState 'hidden' regardless of focus. This suspends requestAnimationFrame (and therefore the R3F Canvas's own internal mount/render pipeline) until a frame is externally forced (a screenshot capture). HTMLMediaElement playback and React effect commits are NOT throttled by this — only Canvas-tree mounting and useFrame-driven updates are. Consistent with the same limitation documented in docs/DRIFT_3D_RUNTIME_BASELINE.md.

limitations: The 500ms extrapolation cap and the extrapolation formula itself are exercised by the pure unit-level logic in src/lib/drift3dAudioClock.ts, but this browser session did not independently time-box a live extrapolation window beyond what §9.3/§9.4 show (pause-freeze and resume-continuity) — no separate stopwatch-style measurement of the extrapolation ceiling was captured live.

No screenshot binaries were committed under this directory for the same reason documented in docs/DRIFT_3D_RUNTIME_BASELINE.md (the save_to_disk mechanism captures an unrelated fixed desktop image, not the driven tab's content) — one screenshot was reviewed live in-session (zone entry, §9.9) confirming HUD/canvas/scene correctness, not persisted as a file.

section14 (correction round): the transient 'seeking' playbackState during Test A was not captured live — seeked resolution on an already-buffered local file (readyState 4) is faster than this session's browser-control round-trip latency. Verified by code reading of onSeeking/onSeeked instead (which unconditionally sets playbackState:'seeking' and never bumps timelineRevision for that reason) rather than by a live transient snapshot.

section14 (correction round): window.__drift3dAudioClock (the Drift3DScene dev probe, gated behind the R3F Canvas mount and therefore requestAnimationFrame) was unreachable in this session — rAF never fired even after the frame-forcing techniques (screenshot capture) that worked earlier in this same lot's troubleshooting became themselves unresponsive. Worked around by reading the same underlying audioClockRef.current directly via React fiber traversal from the <audio> DOM node, which does not depend on Canvas mounting or rAF. This is a read-only introspection technique; no application code was changed to enable it.

section15_correctionRound2_restartOrderi.fix: applyClockRestart now patches { anchorTimeSeconds: 0, playbackState: 'seeking' } in one synchronous updateDrift3DAudioClock call. playPrevious and playTrack's same-track branch now call applyClockRestart() before mutating audio.currentTime (playTrack's branch also gained an explicit setCurrentTime(0), previously missing there).
